summary:
We developed Lunar Outpost: Mission 01, an educational 2D top-down lunar habitat simulator built in Godot 4 and playable instantly in any web browser. Players take command as a Junior Astronaut accompanied by a space pet, managing five core base facilities—Power, Life Support, Greenhouse, Radiation Shelter, and Communications—across a 10-day survival campaign.

Addressing the challenge to inspire young explorers (ages 7–12), the game translates authentic aerospace concepts into accessible, kid-friendly mechanics. Instead of complex math, players navigate resource balances using intuitive trend indicators, smart coach tips, and real-time shelter sprints during emergency solar storms. Real NASA DONKI solar flare records drive space weather events and radio blackouts, while 17 NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) study records provide daily science briefings alongside realistic Earth communication delays.

This project is important because it connects the next generation directly to real Artemis-era lunar science. By delivering a zero-install web experience playable on any school Chromebook, tablet, or phone, it makes STEM education engaging, accessible, and inspiring.
details:
Project Details

  • What It Does & How It Works:
    Lunar Outpost: Mission 01 is an educational 2D top-down simulation game where players step into the boots of a Junior Astronaut managing five base modules—Power Station, Life Support, Hydroponic Greenhouse, Radiation Shelter, and Communications—across a 10-day lunar survival campaign. Players allocate daily Action Points to balance electricity, oxygen, food, water, and realistic multi-day radio delays to Earth, while surviving real-time emergency sprints into the radiation bunker during solar storms.
  • Benefits & Intended Impact:
    Designed for youth (ages 7–12), the game demystifies complex space science without tedious math. Players rely on intuitive trend indicators (+ Going up, - Going down, = Steady), color-coded statuses, and an interactive "Tap-to-Explain" science glossary. It fosters systems thinking and resource conservation to inspire the next generation of Artemis-era STEM leaders.
  • Tools & Technologies:
    Developed in Godot 4 using GDScript, exported to single-threaded WebAssembly/HTML5 with Web Audio Worklets, and hosted on GitHub Pages. All systems are driven by local JSON datasets containing game rules, cached NASA DONKI solar flare telemetry, and 17 NASA OSDR space biology study records.
  • Creativity & Key Considerations:
    Features an animated space pet companion, heart-pounding emergency storm countdowns, and handcrafted procedural vector UI badges. Built with universal accessibility as a priority, the game runs instantly with zero downloads, logins, or fees across school Chromebooks, tablets, smartphones, and desktop PCs.
